dMod2 [@kaschek2019dmod] minimizes $-2 \log L$ (with a prior, $-2 \log$ of the posterior) by the
trust-region method `trust()`, from many starts by `mstrust()`, here on the model of
[Setting up models](guide-model.html) with the gauge of [Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html).
Derivations: [Methods > Trust-region optimization](methods-trust.html).

## Trust-region method

Each iteration minimizes a quadratic model inside a ball of radius $r$, first `rinit`; the ratio
of actual to predicted decrease decides on step and radius. A trial point where the objective fails
counts as rejected. `stepControl$nonmonotone` in $(0, 1)$ also accepts rising steps and returns the
best iterate.

`parlower` and `parupper` set bounds. `boundary = "reflective"` (default) keeps the iterates
strictly inside and lists bound parameters in `atBound`; `boundary = "clip"` removes them from the
subproblem and runs Gauss-Newton only, with `ftol` and `mtol`.

### Termination criteria

`stopReason` names the test that ended the run:

| `stopReason` | test | `converged` |
|---|---|---|
| `"gradient"` | largest gradient entry, scaled by the distance to a bound, at most `gtol` | `TRUE` |
| `"fvalue"` | an accepted step changed the value by less than `ftol` | `TRUE` |
| `"preddiff"` | predicted decrease below `mtol` | `TRUE` |
| `"step"` | step norm below `xtol` (default 0, off) | `TRUE` |
| `"stagnation"` | five rejected steps in a row, value flat within `ftol` | `TRUE` where the full Newton step predicts at most `mtol` |
| `"radius"` | radius below `rmin`, or a step that no longer changes the parameters | `FALSE` |
| `"objfun"` | three failed evaluations in a row | `FALSE` |
| `"iterlim"` | `iterlim` iterations | `FALSE` |

`"gradient"`, `"fvalue"` and `"preddiff"` stop only where the full Newton step also predicts at
most `mtol` ([Methods > Termination criteria](methods-trust.html#termination-criteria)). `ftol`
and `gtol` belong at or above the numerical error; `model.R` defines them as `tolerances`, passed
as `tolControl`.

## Model Hessian

| `hessianMethod` | model Hessian | the objective returns |
|---|---|---|
| `"gn"` | Gauss-Newton | value, gradient, Gauss-Newton Hessian |
| `"exact"` | exact (Newton) | value, gradient, exact Hessian |
| `"bfgs"` | damped BFGS update, positive definite | value, gradient |
| `"sr1"` | symmetric rank-one update, possibly indefinite | value, gradient |

The default is the hybrid of Fides [@froehlich2022fides]: Gauss-Newton until the radius stayed the
same for 20 iterations, then BFGS
([Methods > Hessian phases](methods-trust.html#hessian-phases)).
The sparse path, multiple shooting and `boundary = "clip"` run Gauss-Newton. With an error model the
Gauss-Newton Hessian can be indefinite
([Methods > Gauss-Newton with an error model](methods-sensitivities.html#gauss-newton-with-an-error-model)).
`"exact"` needs a chain built with `derivMode = "forward-forward"` or `"forward-reverse"`
([Sensitivities](guide-sensitivities.html)).
Quasi-Newton settings, entries of `qnControl`:

| entry | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `hessianInit` | `"gn"` | seed: `"gn"`, `"identity"`, `"exact"`, or `"tracked"` (later phases) |
| `hessianReseed` | `"never"` | `"stall"`: reseed instead of stopping on stagnation, up to 8 times |
| `qnMemory` | `0` | `0` accumulates all updates; $m > 0$ rebuilds from the last $m$ pairs |
| `qnCautious` | `1e-8` | cautious test of BFGS; `0` turns it off |
| `qnRejected` | `TRUE` for `"sr1"` | SR1 also updates from rejected trial points |

### Hessian phases and reverse sweep

`phases` runs several sources in turn, each a list with `hessianMethod` and optionally `iterlim`,
`radiusStall`, `sweep`, `keepRadius`, `onStop` and `qnControl`. A phase hands over on a stop other
than `"gradient"`, on `iterlim` or after `radiusStall` iterations at one radius; `switches` bounds
the handovers.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit <- trust(obj, best, fixed = gauge, tolControl = tolerances,
             phases = list(list(hessianMethod = "gn"), list(hessianMethod = "sr1")))
fit[c("phaseIterations", "evalBySource", "nSwitch", "stopReason")]
```

`sweep = "reverse"` computes the gradient of a quasi-Newton phase by one backward sweep, for models
built with `derivMode = c("forward", "reverse")`; a `"bfgs"` or `"sr1"` phase does so by default.

### Sparse Hessians

`sparse = TRUE` uses sparse Cholesky factors, plus a low-rank part, for many parameters that each
act on few conditions; it reaches the same fit as the dense path. `"auto"` (default) takes it from
100 parameters on where it costs fewer flops (`options(dMod2.sparseAuto = )`).

### Arguments and result

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `rinit`, `rmax` | `0.1`, `10` | first and largest radius |
| `iterlim` | `1000` | iterations over all phases |
| `hessianMethod` | Gauss-Newton, then BFGS | source of the model Hessian |
| `phases`, `switches` | none | several sources in turn |
| `parlower`, `parupper`, `boundary` | none, `"reflective"` | bounds |
| `tolControl` | `ftol`, `mtol`, `gtol` `1e-6`; `xtol`, `rmin` `0`; `ctol` `1e-6` | termination; `ctol` for multiple shooting |
| `qnControl` | see above | quasi-Newton update |
| `stepControl` | `thetaMax = 0.99995`, `nonmonotone = 0` | step; further entries for multiple shooting |
| `minimize` | `TRUE` | `FALSE` maximizes |
| `sparse` | `"auto"` | sparse path |
| `blather`, `printIter`, `traceFile` | `FALSE`, `FALSE`, none | trace in the result, printed values, CSV log |

Other arguments go to the objective, such as `fixed`. The `trustfit` holds `argument`, `value`,
`gradient`, `hessian`, `iterations`, `converged`, `atBound` and `stopReason`.

## Multistart fitting

`mstrust()` fits from many starts; `as.parframe()` sorts the fits by value. `fit.R` draws 200
starts from the prior of [Setting up models](guide-model.html#likelihood-and-prior):

```{r multistart, eval = FALSE}
```

Arguments go by name to `trust()`, the sampler or the objective; `set.seed()` reproduces a run for
any `cores`.

| argument | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `center` | | center of the starts, or a parframe of starts |
| `fits` | `20` | number of fits |
| `samplefun` | `"rnorm"` | sampler of the offsets |
| `startFromCenter` | `FALSE` | first fit starts at `center` |
| `retry`, `nTries` | `TRUE`, `10` | a failed fit restarts from the next draw |
| `cores` | `1` | parallel fits, or `c(fits = , conditions = )` |
| `optmethod` | `"trust"` | optimizer, e.g. `"trustL1"` |
| `output`, `cautiousMode` | `FALSE` | write fits to `resultPath` during the run |

`msParframe()` draws shareable starts; `load.parlist()` reads the fits of a running or aborted
run. The fits of `fit.R` ([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html)) are loaded from
`results/fits.rds`:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R"))
```

```{r load}
```

```{r}
c(fits = nrow(fits), converged = sum(fits$converged), best = min(fits$value),
  withinOne = sum(fits$value < min(fits$value) + 1))
```

Sorted values; each plateau is a local optimum:

```{r waterfall, fig.height = 3.5}
```

Parameters that differ by more than 0.1 between the plateaus within 5 of the best:

```{r}
pl <- plotPars(fits, value < min(value) + 5)
med <- with(pl$data, tapply(parvalue, list(name, step), median))
differ <- rownames(med)[apply(med, 1, function(m) diff(range(m, na.rm = TRUE))) > 0.1]
pl$data <- subset(pl$data, name %in% differ)
```

```{r, fig.height = 1 + 0.22 * length(differ)}
pl +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log value", color = "plateau")
```

## Comparison of Hessian sources

`optimizers.R` fits from the same 100 starts with several Hessian sources, loaded from
`results/optimizers.rds`. `hits` counts the fits within 5 of the best value:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/optimizers.rds", "optimizers.R"))
```

```{r}
opt <- readRDS("results/optimizers.rds")
top <- min(opt$value, na.rm = TRUE)
shown <- c("default (Fides hybrid)", "Gauss-Newton", "BFGS", "exact", "GN, then BFGS", "GN, then BFGS at stall 50", "SSR1, scaled",
           "GNSBFGS")
opt <- opt[opt$method %in% shown, ]
method <- factor(opt$method, shown)
t(rbind(converged = tapply(opt$converged, method, sum),
        hits = tapply(opt$value < top + 5, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE),
        secondsPerHit = round(tapply(opt$elapsed, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE) /
                              tapply(opt$value < top + 5, method, sum, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

The exact Hessian converges most often, scaled SR1 reaches the best plateaus most often, and
Gauss-Newton followed by BFGS on the reverse gradient needs the least time per hit. Details:
[Methods > Forward and reverse derivatives on the Oppelt fit](methods-trust.html#forward-and-reverse-derivatives-on-the-oppelt-fit).

## L1 penalties

`trustL1()` adds $\sum_i \lambda_i \lvert \theta_i - \mu_i \rvert$ for the parameters named in
`mu`; a scan over `lambda` selects the parameters that differ from the reference. `one.sided`,
`gate` and `fuse` vary the penalty ([Methods > L1 penalties](methods-trust.html#l1-penalties)).

Multiple shooting for oscillating or spiking systems:
[Methods > Multiple shooting](methods-multiple-shooting.html).

`plotValues()`, `plotPars()`, `normL2()`
